text:
aj: Heads-up — after flipping cross-warp serialization + FP8 on the L40S pool we saw a clear perf spike and some tail regressions :grimacing:

aj: Here's the quick repro we used (local trace):
```
$ ./run_infer --model=mosaic-13b-fp8 --device=l40s --te-flag=TE_ENABLE_CROSSWARP_SERIALIZE=1 --batch=8 --kv-mode=hotcache
... logs ...
p50=42ms p95=318ms throughput=220 tok/s per-gpu
```

aj: Baseline (same load, crosswarp off): p50=36ms p95=180ms throughput=310 tok/s. CPU+PCI stalls visible in trace.

maria: Interesting — so enabling the TE serialize path dropped throughput by ~30% and doubled p95. Did kernel selection flip to the narrow-int8-fused path or to the fp8-serial kernel?

aj: It looks like the runtime elected the fp8_crosswarp_serialize kernel (fallback chain: fp8_vectorized -> fp8_crosswarp_serialize) because occupancy heuristics thought it would reduce memory contention for long contexts.

ken: @aj can you paste the small perf counters from the profiler (sm__* / l1/lsl)?

aj: pasted snippet from nvprof flame: 
```
SMUtil: 78% -> 92% spikes
L1_local_hit_rate: 0.61 -> 0.32
PCIe_writes_stall: +120ms
CUDA_l2_requests: +18%
```

aj: The crosswarp kernel serializes warps to lower active SM usage but increases PCIe flushes due to how we stage KV chunks; that matches the L1 drop.

sara: Any KV cache eviction churn? hotcache mode should keep prefix cached but serialization changes chunking alignment.

aj: Yes — KV trace shows more micro-evictions during long-context tails. Eviction count +67% vs baseline. Likely due to chunk boundary fragmentation when we serialize across warps.

xavier: Could this be an L40S-specific memory/SM scheduling artifact? H100 has larger L2 and different cross-warp intrinsics. Do we see same on H100?

aj: H100 test run: with same flags throughput drop was smaller (310 -> 270 tok/s) and p95 moved 160 -> 210ms. So H100 is more tolerant, L40S hit worse.

maria: That suggests we need a device-aware selector: prefer crosswarp_serialize only for H100 or for models with short seq-lens. Also we should tweak batching heuristics: lower microbatch size when serialize is on so we don't bloat KV chunking.

ken: Agreed. Quick mitigation: roll back TE_ENABLE_CROSSWARP_SERIALIZE for L40S pools and enable auto-fallback to fp8_vectorized when eviction_rate>5% in last 5m.

deploy-bot: rollout request by @ken: revert TE_ENABLE_CROSSWARP_SERIALIZE for production/l40s at 2026-03-12T17:22:00Z — status: queued

aj: For long-term fix I propose:
- Add a kernel-scoring metric that includes KV_eviction_rate and PCIe_stall_delta.
- Adjust batching heuristic to prefer smaller per-GPU batch when crosswarp is chosen.
- Add an FP8 calibration stage to prefer slightly higher dynamic range quant stats for L40S (reduce saturation).

sara: On calibration: we saw earlier that tighter FP8 calibration reduced numeric noise but slowed kernels due to extra normalization passes. Need to measure quality delta vs perf. Maybe run A/B with our eval prompt set.

xavier: Also try INT8 fallback for tail requests (when seq_len>1024) — INT8 vectorized kernel keeps KV chunk boundaries consistent.

maria: I'll open a PR for selector change and a small e2e test harness to reproduce eviction spike. If anyone has a repro script or flame id, drop it here.

aj: Repro artifact: trace id flame-239444-07 (S3) and a short wrapper: `scripts/repro/crosswarp_kv_spike.sh` — uses 50 requests with mixed seq-lens.

ken: Thanks. I'll watch the rollback rollout and start the selector PR review. :eyes:

maria: Great, thx everyone. We'll coordinate on the canary once the selector PR lands.

aj: TL;DR — cross-warp serialize + FP8 triggered KV fragmentation on L40S causing PCIe stalls and p95 regressions. Mitigate by rolling back on L40S, add device-aware kernel scoring, tweak batching and calibration.
